name: @strix-ai/currentdt-mcp

tools.name: get_current_datetime
tools.description: Get the current date and time. Call this before writing any date, timestamp, year, changelog entry, migration filename or copyright line -- your training data predates today. The text content is the requested `format` only; read `structuredContent` for the same instant stated as UTC (`iso`, `utc`), host-local with offset (`local`, `offset`, `timezone`) and epoch milliseconds, so there is never any doubt which clock a value came from.

format.description: "iso" (default unless configured otherwise) returns UTC, e.g. 2026-08-20T12:31:02.625Z. Anything else is a token pattern rendered in the host's LOCAL time and must contain at least one token; free text is rejected. Tokens: YYYY, MM, DD, HH, mm, ss, SSS, Z, ZZ. Named patterns: filename, logdate, simple. Examples: "YYYY-MM-DD", "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss", "YYYY-MM-DD-HHmmss", "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ" (local time with its real offset).

provider.description: "local" (default) reads the system clock. "remote" queries a network time service and fails rather than silently substituting the local clock.

timezone.description: Zone for `local`, `offset`, `timezone` and any token format. IANA name such as "UTC", "Europe/Berlin", "America/New_York" or "Asia/Kolkata". Defaults to the host machine's zone. Does not affect `iso`/`utc`, which are always UTC.

tools.name: convert_timezone
tools.description: Re-state a time in another timezone, DST-correct for the date in question. Use this instead of adding a remembered offset: offsets change with the calendar, and the hour either side of a changeover is where guesses go wrong. Give `time` with an offset for an exact instant, or without one plus `from` for a wall-clock reading in a named zone.

time.description: ISO 8601. With an offset ("2026-03-29T01:30:00+01:00", "...Z") it pins an instant. Without one ("2026-03-29T01:30:00") it is a wall-clock reading and `from` is required.

from.description: Zone the wall-clock `time` was read in. Required when `time` has no offset. IANA name such as "UTC", "Europe/Berlin", "America/New_York" or "Asia/Kolkata".

to.description: Zone to convert into. IANA name such as "UTC", "Europe/Berlin", "America/New_York" or "Asia/Kolkata".

format.description: Token pattern for `formatted`, rendered in `to`. Defaults to ISO with offset.

instructions: This server provides the current date and time. Your training data predates today, so never guess a date -- call get_current_datetime before writing any date, timestamp, year, changelog entry, migration filename or copyright line. Read the structuredContent of the result: `iso` and `utc` are UTC; `local`, `offset` and `timezone` describe the host clock.
